questions.q: What does a span represent in distributed tracing?
options: An entire trace from start to finish
One unit of work — such as one HTTP call or database query — with a start time, duration, and attributes
A log level like error or warn
A dashboard panel in Grafana
questions.explain: A span is the smallest unit in a trace: one operation, with timing and key-value attributes describing it.

questions.q: How does a trace reconstruct the full call tree of a request?
options: Every span shares a trace ID, and each span's parent_span_id links it to the span that called it
By sorting log lines alphabetically
By storing every span in a separate database per service
Traces don't track relationships between spans
questions.explain: A shared trace_id groups all spans belonging to one request, while parent_span_id on each span reconstructs exactly which call happened inside which.

options: The exact dashboard layout every team must use
Vendor-neutral APIs/SDKs, a wire protocol (OTLP), and an optional Collector for routing telemetry
Which cloud provider you must use for hosting
The specific colors used in trace waterfall views
questions.explain: OpenTelemetry standardizes instrumentation (APIs/SDKs), the OTLP wire protocol, and the Collector — so applications can be instrumented once and sent to any compatible backend.

questions.q: In a trace waterfall view like Jaeger's, what does a wide bar typically indicate?
options: A span that used more memory
A span that ran earlier in the trace
A span with a longer duration — often the first place to look when investigating slowness
A span that failed with an error
questions.explain: Bar width in a waterfall is proportional to span duration, so the widest bar is the slowest step — exactly where an engineer should start investigating a latency spike.

questions.q: Why would Northbridge's engineering team instrument the checkout service with OpenTelemetry instead of a vendor-specific tracing SDK?
options: OpenTelemetry is the only option that supports JSON
They can switch or add trace backends (Jaeger, Tempo, a commercial vendor) later by changing only exporter configuration, not application code
Vendor-specific SDKs don't support distributed tracing
OpenTelemetry eliminates the need for trace IDs
questions.explain: Because OTel standardizes the instrumentation layer separately from the backend, teams avoid vendor lock-in — the same instrumented code can export to any OTLP-compatible backend.
